prompt: Mid-case: A manufacturer wants to cut costs 10%. You've found that materials are 50% of costs and that renegotiating could cut them 8%, saving 4% of total costs. You also learned the products are made in Ohio. You haven't looked at labor, which is 30% of costs. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: renegotiating materials would cut them 8%, nearly reaching the 10% target on its own.
options.feedback: An 8% cut on half of costs saves 4% of the total, well short of 10%.

options.text: So far: materials are half of costs at our Ohio plants, and renegotiating could save 4% of total costs. Next, labor.
options.feedback: Where the plants are isn't part of what you found, so it doesn't belong in the summary.

options.text: So far: materials and labor together could cut about 8% of costs, close to the target.
options.feedback: Labor hasn't been looked at yet.

options.text: So far: an 8% cut on materials, half of costs, saves about 4% of the total. Labor, 30% of costs, comes next.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open.

explanation: Known: an 8% cut on materials, half of costs, saves 4% of total costs. Open: labor, 30% of costs, to close the remaining 6%. Next: look for labor savings. If labor can't deliver about 6%, the target needs other cost lines too.

irrelevant_facts: The company makes its products in Ohio.
